title: Tea-Horse Station
premise: A long drama at a Sichuan-Tibet Tea-Horse Road station. Caravan boss Cheng Yuan and tea worker Xiaoman guard the official tea brand; Xiaoman and A-Du look nearly identical but wear different wrist guards; tea packhorse Qiuli falls to its death and must be avoided; the tea-horse tax ledger, count memory, and temporal flashbacks run throughout. Human-readable context only; never fed to the SUT.

states.prime_boss: A forty-year-old tea-caravan boss, dark-red headwrap, sheepskin jacket, copper scale-weight and horsewhip at the waist, booming voice, hands calloused by tea ropes.
states.lame_from_kick: The same Cheng Yuan: left leg kicked by a horse, limping on a broken whip, sheepskin jacket mud-spotted, copper scale-weight still at the waist.
states.died_at_office: Cheng Yuan has closed his eyes in death, lying still on the tea-office earthen kang, sheepskin jacket covering his chest, broken whip leaning by the bed.

states.young_worker: A fifteen-year-old tea-worker girl, indigo waist sash, coral stud in the left ear, tea rope often wound on her wrist, bright clear eyes.
states.adult_boss: A woman caravan boss in her early twenties, still in indigo waist sash and coral stud, tall and upright, palm marked by brand burns.

states.intact: A copper official tea brand issued by the government, the two characters 'Border Tea' clear on the face, long handle wrapped in deep-brown leather strip.
states.cracked_seal: The same official tea brand, face cracked, the 'Border' character incomplete, deep-brown leather on the handle loose and curled.
states.recast: After recasting, the official tea brand's inscription is complete again, new copper a shade brighter, long handle rewrapped tight in deep-brown leather.

states.intact: A cowhide-covered tea-horse tax ledger recording tea-brick counts, fodder accounts, porter silver, and mountain-pass clearance dates.
states.tea_stained: The same tea-horse tax ledger soaked through with strong tea, cowhide cover sticky, vermilion numbers blurred into brown clumps.

states.intact: A date-red tea packhorse named Qiuli, border-tea brand burned into the saddle flaps, symmetric tea-brick packs on both sides.
states.fallen_dead: Tea packhorse Qiuli has fallen dead on a steep slope, saddle flaps torn, tea-brick packs scattered, border-tea brand mark still clear.

states.young_rival: A young caravan bookkeeper nearly identical in face to Xiaoman, but wearing silver-gray wrist guards and an ochre waist sash, cold hard eyes.
states.disguised: Disguised A-Du still wears silver-gray wrist guards, a knife scar now at the brow, ochre sash replaced by an old leather belt.

segments.action: At dusk, tea-caravan boss Cheng Yuan lifts the thick cotton door curtain into the tea warehouse hall and sets the official tea brand by a small stove to preheat.
Five butter lamps hang under the tea-warehouse hall beams; Cheng Yuan trims each wick in turn, light falling on stacked tea bricks.
Two copper horse bells hang inside the door beam; Cheng Yuan taps them with a knuckle, and the ring carries through the hall.
Cheng Yuan presses the official tea brand onto damp cotton to test the heat; the characters 'Border Tea' rise clear in white steam.
Cheng Yuan unties a leather cord, opens the cowhide-covered tea-horse tax ledger, and checks tomorrow's tea-brick count for the mountain pass.
He looks up and counts the five butter lamps under the beams, confirming enough light before sealing the tea for the night.
Cheng Yuan sets the official tea brand beside the tea-horse tax ledger, ready to brand each pack after the mouths are sealed.
In the morning hitching yard, Cheng Yuan greets young Xiaoman leading tea packhorse Qiuli, tea-brick packs hanging full on both sides of the saddle.

segments.action: Months later on a mountain-rain night, Cheng Yuan keeps the fire alone in the tea warehouse hall; the official tea brand by the stove glows faintly red.
A bowl of strong tea is knocked over by the wind; the tea-horse tax ledger is soaked through, vermilion numbers blurred into brown clumps.

segments.action: The spring tea season stretches long; every day Cheng Yuan weighs newly pressed tea bricks in the tea warehouse hall.
Before the Start of Summer, Cheng Yuan beats dust from saddle pads at the doorway; mountain-pass fog clings to the stone steps.
At autumn harvest, the caravan sorts damp tea packs in the hall; Cheng Yuan never takes his eyes off the branding furnace.
On a snowy night, Cheng Yuan wraps his sheepskin jacket tight and listens to distant horse-train bells drawing near.
Another New Year's Eve, only furnace fire and rows of tea bricks remain in the warehouse; Cheng Yuan locks the brand into an iron box.
At dawn, Cheng Yuan patrols the hitching yard; tea packhorse Qiuli grazes with head down, paired tea packs still hanging at the saddle.
Cheng Yuan bends to check Qiuli's shoes, girth, and saddle-flap brand mark.
He returns to the tea-warehouse desk and confirms those three tea-brick samples are still ranked by shade.
A gray mule is led in by a porter, salt bags on its back, saddle flaps without a border-tea brand.
Afternoon storm pins the mountain pass; mud floods the hitching yard; the caravan hurries tea packs into the warehouse.
Cheng Yuan rushes over the threshold clutching the official tea brand; the copper seal strikes a stone step and a crack bursts across the face.

segments.action: Toward the pass, tea packhorse Qiuli charges with the last two tea-brick packs; the stone underfoot suddenly loosens.
Down the steep slope, tea packhorse Qiuli tumbles and falls dead; saddle flaps tear, tea-brick packs roll into the rain ditch.

segments.action: Qiuli's torn girth is hung on the tea-warehouse wall; Cheng Yuan stares a long time at that scrap of old leather.
Cheng Yuan packs Qiuli's saddle-flap shards into a wooden box, leaving only the brand mark face-up.
The five butter lamps under the beams remain; Cheng Yuan takes one to light Qiuli's old nameplate.
The cracked official tea brand lies on the desk; Cheng Yuan adds another line to the ledger for Qiuli's loss.

segments.action: A porter carries a back-basket frame into the hitching yard, clay jars and straw rope bound on top—no saddle, no tea-brick packs.
A tea-tax clerk walks in, also in a dark-red headwrap, but the official plaque on his chest swings plainly.
The tea-tax clerk points at the back-basket frame to check bamboo tallies; Cheng Yuan only tucks the recast official tea brand back to his waist.

segments.action: From the kitchen comes a tea girl in a light-brown waist sash; her profile at a glance looks like young Xiaoman, but she wears green glass earrings.
The tea girl practices coiling tea rope; Cheng Yuan reads her shy eyes and shakes his head, sending her to add firewood.
Years later at dusk, after a startled horse kicks him, Cheng Yuan limps on a broken whip to the abandoned tea-horse office door.
